tasks.title: packaging: the Linux x64 platform package and the launcher shim

details.goal: npm i -g sangkar-mcp must install a native binary on Linux x64 with no Bun and no build step, and must refuse every other platform by name instead of failing obscurely.
details.contract:
The first Rust release targets ONE platform: `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`.
`package.json`: keep the name `sangkar-mcp` and the current version; `bin` becomes `{"sangkar": "bin/sangkar.js"}`; `files` becomes `["bin", "agent", "README.md"]`; `optionalDependencies` declares exactly one entry, `sangkar-mcp-linux-x64-gnu`, pinned to the SAME version as the parent; `engines` becomes `{"node": ">=18"}` (the shim only — the server is native); remove every `scripts` entry that invokes bun/tsc/biome/drizzle.
`bin/sangkar.js`: `#!/usr/bin/env node`, CommonJS, no dependencies. It resolves a platform key from `process.platform` + `process.arch` and needs exactly one mapping for now (`linux:x64` -> `sangkar-mcp-linux-x64-gnu`). If the key is not that one, or the package is not installed, it prints ONE stderr line and exits 70, naming: the key it wanted, the single published platform, and the version to pin to stay on the TypeScript build (`sangkar-mcp@<the current beta line>`). Otherwise it `spawnSync`s `<pkg>/bin/sangkar` with `stdio: 'inherit'`, forwarding every argv byte, and exits with the child's code. Forward SIGINT/SIGTERM to the child.
The key table is DATA (one map plus one refusal string) so adding macOS or Windows later is one entry, one `npm/<key>/` directory and one release-matrix row — never a rewrite.
`rust/scripts/package.sh`: `cargo build --release --locked -p sangkar-cli --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `strip`, then lay out `npm/linux-x64-gnu/bin/sangkar` and `npm/linux-x64-gnu/package.json` with `{"name", "version", "os": ["linux"], "cpu": ["x64"], "files": ["bin"], "license": "MIT", "repository"}` consistent with the parent.
`npm/` holds the generated layout, committed as a template for the release workflow (the workflow fills the version).
Verify on this machine only (Linux x64): `node bin/sangkar.js status --repo-root rust/tests/parity/fixtures/polyglot --data-dir <temp>` answers, and moving `node_modules/sangkar-mcp-linux-x64-gnu` aside makes the shim exit 70 with the one-line refusal.
steps: Rewrite package.json (name/version kept, bin, files, ONE optionalDependency, engines, scripts pruned).
Write bin/sangkar.js with the one-entry key table, the refusal line and signal forwarding.
Write rust/scripts/package.sh for the single target and generate npm/linux-x64-gnu/.
Build, run the shim against a fixture, then rename the platform package aside and record the refusal.

tasks.title: CI and release: one target, artifacts, no npm publish

details.goal: Every push checks formatting, lints and tests on the pinned toolchain; a tag builds the single Linux x64 binary and attaches it, leaving the npm publish to the maintainer (it needs an OTP).
details.contract:
`.github/workflows/ci.yml`: on push/PR — `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` on `ubuntu-latest` with `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.100.0` and a `Swatinem/rust-cache` step. `git` must be available for the diff tests. One job only: a macOS job lands with the macOS release (open question 3 is answered "Linux x64 first"), and adding it later must be an extension of this file, not a rewrite.
`.github/workflows/release.yml`: `workflow_dispatch` plus `push: tags: ['v*']`; ONE target, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, built on `ubuntu-22.04` because that image decides the glibc floor (2.35) — record the floor in a comment and in the release notes; `cargo build --release --locked`; run `rust/scripts/package.sh`; upload the platform package as an artifact; create a GitHub Release on a tag and attach the tarball plus the platform `.tgz`. Do NOT run `npm publish` in CI — the release notes say the maintainer publishes TWO packages by hand in order (the platform package first, then the parent), matching `.agents/skills/build-n-deploy`.
Keep both files minimal: no matrix of Rust versions, no `cargo-audit`, no cache keys that expire silently.

Write release.yml with the one target, the glibc comment and the artifact upload.
Add the step that creates the GitHub Release on a tag.
